newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks shoot up, inspired by rate cut, U.S.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks shoot up, inspired by rate cut, U.S.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed markedly higher on Tuesday after lower-than-expected U.S. inflation this afternoon added to optimism on a domestic rate cut this morning.
The general index rose 2.23 percent, 10.63 points, to 487.07 and the Ibex-35 added 133.29 points, 2.44 percent, to 5,585.85.
Telefonica added 70 pesetas to 3,505 after Portugal Telecom confirmed a share swap deal, raising analyst expectations of an deal with MCI in the U.S.
Repsol rose 110 pesetas to a new high at 6,190 amid this month's public share offering.
Endesa outperformed, adding 300 pesetas to 9,400, recovering after recent weakness, dealers said.
Dealers said the bouse has been looking to move higher since better-than-expected March inflation and an improved economic outlook became apparent. But Wall Street had been holding the market back.
"When the U.S. market pushes higher at last we see that we can recover what we should have done before based on our own good economic fundamentals," said a trader at a Spanish bank.
Today's 25 basis points cut in the Bank of Spain's key money market rate to 5.50 percent was widely expected, but prospects for more cuts later this year are instilling optimism, he added.
